AlternateTargets: copying another's way and losing one's own
SearchAliases: copying another's way and losing one's own
Senses.Note: This allusive use differs from the actual place and the personal title below. Tang-gait, Handan-gait, imitation, and former-gait variants belong to one walking-imitation family, but their grammatical actors must not be silently interchanged.

Occurrences.Kwic: 清云：邯鄲學唐步。雪竇顯云：這僧不是邯鄲人，為甚學唐步？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Old Cases Raised in the Lineage (宗門拈古彙集), in the comments on Zhaozhou Congshen's tea case: Jingqing Daofu gives the first exact headword verdict after the unnamed monk leaves; Xuedou Chongxian repeats the headword in the immediately following comment.

Occurrences.Kwic: 脚下若參差，邯鄲學唐步。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): in Xichan Wenlian's explicitly headed section, Xichan Wenlian warns that if one's footing is off, one resembles the Handan walker imitating another gait.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不可在語脈裡轉嫫母效顰邯鄲學步見笑大方取譏識者
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of National Master Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄): Yulin Tongxiu warns that examining public cases by turning inside their verbal thread is like the ugly woman imitating a frown or learning the Handan walk, inviting ridicule from knowledgeable people.

Occurrences.Kwic: 打失衲僧鼻孔，忘却邯鄲故步。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Correct Lineage of the Continuation of the Lamp (續燈正統): inside Sanyi Mingyu's explicitly headed small address, Sanyi says that patch-robed monks lose their noses and forget the old Handan gait, then surveys the assembly and says 'exposed.'

Senses.Explanation: A walking-imitation allusion used as a verdict on derivative conduct: someone copies another gait and may lose the step previously his own. The records preserve two grammatical directions rather than one person called a 'Handan gait-imitator.' In the shorter 'learn the Handan gait' (邯鄲學步), attested eight times in seven allowlisted texts, Handan supplies the gait being copied. In the more frequent Chan formula 'Handan learns the Tang gait' (邯鄲學唐步), attested 48 times in 35 texts, a Handan person instead copies a Tang gait. Jingqing Daofu applies the latter verdict when an unnamed monk walks away after being asked how he understands Zhaozhou Congshen's 'drink tea'; Xuedou Chongxian then asks why someone who is not a Handan man learns the Tang gait. Xichan Wenlian attaches the formula to uneven footing, while Yulin Tongxiu warns that following the verbal thread of public cases becomes 'learning the Handan gait' and invites informed ridicule. Sanyi Mingyu speaks of forgetting Handan's former gait. Chan deployment therefore keeps the walking, imitation, and loss-of-one's-own-step scene visible while reversing who copies whom; those grammatical roles do not create separate lexical things.

Senses.Note: This sense covers the place itself, including when a poem invokes the dream located there. It is secondary because the imitation formula dominates the Chan concordance.

Occurrences.Kwic: 妾家邯鄲住，歌聲亦抑揚
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Yi'an (翼菴禪師語錄): in the collected Hanshan poem, Hanshan's poetic voice says that his home is in Handan and his singing rises and falls.

Occurrences.Kwic: 邯鄲一枕，歷盡榮華五十載，覺來黃粱炊尚未熟
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄): Baichi Yuan, in his inscription on the Record of Lu Sheng's Yellow-Millet Dream (題盧生黃粱夢記), recounts the Handan pillow dream and says that Lu Sheng awoke before the millet was cooked.

Senses.Explanation: The graphs also name the actual city of Handan. One verse says, “my home is in Handan” (妾家邯鄲住). Chan writing also preserves the city as the setting of the yellow-millet dream: “one pillow at Handan: he passed through fifty years of glory; on waking, the yellow millet was not yet cooked” (邯鄲一枕，歷盡榮華五十載，覺來黃粱炊尚未熟). Literal residence and the dream’s setting retain the same geographic referent; the literary allusion does not make a new place.

SearchAliases: Zen Li Shu, Duke of Handan
Senses.Note: This distinct title/person use has one allowlisted source and is therefore provisional. It is not merged into the geographic sense merely because the title contains the place-name.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Pujue Zonggao (普覺宗杲禪師語錄): the biographical compiler's narrative identifies Handan Gong as Li Shu, then aged seven.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The clause is third-person biography rather than a speech turn.

Senses.Explanation: In one biographical passage, “Handan” is part of a personal title rather than the city or imitator: “the Duke of Handan, personal name Shu, was then seven years old” (邯鄲公諱淑，時方七歲). The title identifies the named child in that retrospective.
